nodes.name: Characterisation of proper conditional expectation kernels, Remark 1.20
nodes.statement: Let muinM(X,MCX) be a finite measure and let piinKer_MCB,MCX be a proper kernel. Then, pi is a conditional expectation kernel for mu iff mupi = mu

conclusions: Then, pi is a conditional expectation kernel for mu iff mupi = mu

nodes.statement: By the characterisation of conditional expectation, pi is a conditional expectation kernel for mu iff forall A in MCX, forall B in MCB, mu(A inter B) = int_B pi(A|cdot)\ partialmu By properness of pi, int_B pi(A|cdot)\ partialmu = mupi(A inter B) Hence pi is a cond. exp. kernel with respect to mu & iff forall A in MCX, forall B in MCB, mu(A inter B) = mupi(A inter B) \\ & iff forall A in MCX, mu(A) = mupi(A) \\ & iff mu = mupi
nodes.raw_latex:
By the characterisation of conditional expectation,
    $$\pi \text{ is a conditional expectation kernel for }\mu \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \forall B \in \MCB, \mu(A \inter B) = \int_B \pi(A|\cdot)\ \partial\mu$$
    By properness of $\pi$,
    $$\int_B \pi(A|\cdot)\ \partial\mu = \mu\pi(A \inter B)$$
    Hence
    \begin{align}
        \pi \text{ is a cond. exp. kernel with respect to }\mu
        & \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \forall B \in \MCB, \mu(A \inter B) = \mu\pi(A \inter B) \\
        & \iff \forall A \in \MCX, \mu(A) = \mu\pi(A) \\
        & \iff \mu = \mu\pi
    \end{align}

\label{def:gibbs-meas}

nodes.statement: For all Lambda in Finset(S), A in mathcal E^S, B in F_SsetminusLambda, eta : S to E, we want to prove (rhogamma)_Lambda(A inter B | eta) = 1_B(eta) (rhogamma)_Lambda(A B | eta) Expanding out, this is equivalent to int_zeta in A inter B rho_Lambda(zeta)\ d(gamma_Lambda(eta)) = 1_B(eta) int_zeta in A rho_Lambda(zeta)\ d(gamma_Lambda(eta)) which is true by Lemma with f = 1_Arho_Lambda, g = 1_B.
nodes.raw_latex:
For all $\Lambda \in \Finset(S)$, $A \in \mathcal E^S$, $B \in \mathcal{F}_{S\setminus\Lambda}$, $\eta : S \to E$, we want to prove
    $$(\rho\gamma)_\Lambda(A \inter B | \eta) = 1_B(\eta) (\rho\gamma)_\Lambda(A B | \eta)$$
    Expanding out, this is equivalent to
    $$\int_{\zeta \in A \inter B} \rho_\Lambda(\zeta)\ d(\gamma_\Lambda(\eta)) = 1_B(\eta) \int_{\zeta \in A} \rho_\Lambda(\zeta)\ d(\gamma_\Lambda(\eta))$$
    which is true by Lemma \ref{lem:proper-ker-lintegral} with $f = 1_A\rho_\Lambda$, $g = 1_B$.

nodes.name: Every specification is a modification of some ISSSD, Remark 1.28.5
nodes.statement: If E is countable, nu is the counting measure and gamma is any specification, then rho_Lambda(eta) = gamma_Lambda(\sigma_Lambda = eta_Lambda\ | eta) is a modifier from ISSSD(nu) to gamma.
assumptions: If E is countable, nu is the counting measure and gamma is any specification
conclusions: then rho_Lambda(eta) = gamma_Lambda(\sigma_Lambda = eta_Lambda\ | eta) is a modifier from ISSSD(nu) to gamma.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:exists-modif-isssd}
    
    
    

    If $E$ is countable, $\nu$ is the counting measure and $\gamma$ is any specification, then
    $$\rho_\Lambda(\eta) = \gamma_\Lambda(\{\sigma_\Lambda = \eta_\Lambda\} | \eta)$$
    is a modifier from $\ISSSD(\nu)$ to $\gamma$.
nodes.clean_text: If E is countable, nu is the counting measure and gamma is any specification, then rho_Lambda(eta) = gamma_Lambda(\sigma_Lambda = eta_Lambda\ | eta) is a modifier from ISSSD(nu) to gamma.
nodes.label: lem:exists-modif-isssd

nodes.statement: For all Lambda in Finset(S), A measurable, eta : S to E, we have (rhoISSSD(nu))_Lambda(A|eta) & = int_zeta rho_Lambda(zeta) ISSSD(nu)(dzeta|eta) \\ & = int_zeta gamma_Lambda(\sigma_Lambda = eta_Lambda\ | eta) ISSSD(nu)(dzeta|eta) \\ & = gamma_Lambda(A|eta)
nodes.raw_latex:
For all $\Lambda \in \Finset(S)$, $A$ measurable, $\eta : S \to E$, we have
    \begin{align}
        (\rho\ISSSD(\nu))_\Lambda(A|\eta)
        & = \int_\zeta \rho_\Lambda(\zeta) \ISSSD(\nu)(d\zeta|\eta) \\
        & = \int_\zeta \gamma_\Lambda(\{\sigma_\Lambda = \eta_\Lambda\} | \eta) \ISSSD(\nu)(d\zeta|\eta) \\
        & = \gamma_\Lambda(A|\eta)
    \end{align}

nodes.name: Premodifier, Definition 1.31
nodes.statement: A family of measurable functions h_Lambda : (S to E) to [0, infty[ is a premodifier if h_Lambda_2(zeta)h_Lambda_1(eta) = h_Lambda_1(zeta)h_Lambda_2(eta) for all Lambda_1 subseteq Lambda_2 and all zeta, eta : S to E such that zeta_Lambda_1^c = eta_Lambda_1^c.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:premodif}
    
    
    

    A family of measurable functions $h_\Lambda : (S \to E) \to [0, \infty[$ is a {\bf premodifier} if
    $$h_{\Lambda_2}(\zeta)h_{\Lambda_1}(\eta) = h_{\Lambda_1}(\zeta)h_{\Lambda_2}(\eta)$$
    for all $\Lambda_1 \subseteq \Lambda_2$ and all $\zeta, \eta : S \to E$ such that $\zeta_{\Lambda_1^c} = \eta_{\Lambda_1^c}$.
nodes.clean_text: A family of measurable functions h_Lambda : (S to E) to [0, infty[ is a premodifier if h_Lambda_2(zeta)h_Lambda_1(eta) = h_Lambda_1(zeta)h_Lambda_2(eta) for all Lambda_1 subseteq Lambda_2 and all zeta, eta : S to E such that zeta_Lambda_1^c = eta_Lambda_1^c.
nodes.label: def:premodif

nodes.name: Premodifiers give rise to modifiers, Remark 1.32
nodes.statement: If h is a premodifier and nu is such that 0 < nu_Lambda h_Lambda < infty for all Lambda, then rho_Lambda := frach_LambdaISSSD(nu)_Lambda h_Lambda is a modifier of ISSSD(nu).
assumptions: If h is a premodifier and nu is such that 0 < nu_Lambda h_Lambda < infty for all Lambda
conclusions: then rho_Lambda := frach_LambdaISSSD(nu)_Lambda h_Lambda is a modifier of ISSSD(nu).
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:premodif-modif}
    
    
    
    If $h$ is a premodifier and $\nu$ is such that $0 < \nu_\Lambda h_\Lambda < \infty$ for all $\Lambda$, then
    $$\rho_\Lambda := \frac{h_\Lambda}{\ISSSD(\nu)_\Lambda h_\Lambda}$$
    is a modifier of $\ISSSD(\nu)$.
